purpose: The R-6 baseline response corpus and the primary behavior-parity evidence for the Node 22 / hapi 21 modernization: every parameterless GET route of the unmodified application at the base commit, captured over real HTTP together with the mandatory authenticated supplement, so that the migrated server can be replayed against it and proven to have changed nothing observable.

No pre-migration package was added, removed or overlaid; @hapi/hapi resolved to the base 20.3.0. A clone rather than a `git archive` export precisely so the capture is ATTRIBUTABLE: capture.js reads `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` in the tree it is measuring and refuses to write unless HEAD is metadata.baseCommit with zero MODIFIED tracked files. The untracked paths that remain -- the copied harness, node_modules/ and the hydrated public/components -- are recorded in metadata.gitState.untracked rather than tolerated silently.
metadata.gitStatusCleanScope: tracked files only, in both the capture checkout and the repository working tree
metadata.gitStatusNote: Explicit statement of what gitStatusClean asserts, so it cannot be read as contradicting the untracked paths: ZERO tracked files differed. In the isolated capture checkout every one of the 520 tracked files of 2f8712a was verified byte-identical to the commit, and its only untracked paths were node_modules/ (produced by npm ci from the base lockfile) and the throwaway harness. datastoreState.rationale: Recorded because this corpus is NOT unconditionally independent of persisted state. The eleven GET /<lang> landing rows carry pre [helpers.trinketTypeEnabled, {method: helpers.findFeaturedTrinkets, assign: featuredTrinkets}] (config/routes.js:L551-L570), and findFeaturedTrinkets reaches internals.namedTrinketList -> trinketStore.byCategory (Redis EXISTS + LRANGE on snippets:<lang>:featured, lib/util/store/trinketStore.js) -> Trinket.findByIds (MongoDB). python is the only trinket type enabled in config/default.yaml, so GET /python is the one corpus row that actually performs that read and returns 200; the other ten short-circuit to 404 at trinketTypeEnabled before the featured pre-handler runs. The authenticated supplement reads state too: pages.home calls Trinket.findRecentByOwner. A reproducible corpus therefore requires the datastore state to be initialized explicitly and recorded, which is what this block does.
datastoreState.isolation: The harness FORCES its own disposable database through NODE_CONFIG (metadata.database, test/baseline/capture.js#resolveDatabase) and validates it before every query and every delete with the same fail-closed gate test/helpers/db.js applies before it drops a database: NODE_ENV must be `test`, the connection must be open, mongoose and the driver must agree on the name, the name must match /^test([_-][A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)?$/, and it must be exactly the name this run forced. An earlier revision of this harness forced nothing, so it inherited whatever node-config finally resolved -- for a developer who followed docs/setup.md, the `trinket` DEVELOPMENT database -- and then deleted documents there by a fixed email. The forced name is per-clone (BASELINE_MONGO_DATABASE, or CLONE_INDEX appended) so parallel clones of this repository under a shared workspace cannot collide, and it is never the `test` database the mocha suite owns, so the capture cannot interfere with that suite's own lifecycle.

mongo.databaseNote: Forced and validated by the harness; disposable by name. Dropped out of band immediately before boot, so the capture starts from the fingerprinted empty state recorded below.
mongo.persistence: the container carries a volume, but this database does not outlive the capture: it is dropped before the run and both throwaway identities are removed in a terminal finally afterwards

redis.logicalIsolation: none available -- config/redis.js reads only db.redis.<role>.{host,port,pass} and exposes no database index, and adding one would be an application change this refactor does not sanction. The instance is therefore SHARED with anything else on the host.
redis.stateThatMatters: Exactly one Redis region reaches this corpus: snippets:<lang>:featured, read by helpers.findFeaturedTrinkets -> trinketStore.byCategory for the eleven GET /<lang> landing rows, of which only /python is enabled. Measured immediately before this capture: `KEYS snippets*` returned NOTHING, so the featured list is empty and /python renders the empty-featured page recorded here. The other keys present on the shared instance (bull:exports:*, courses:<slug>:ids, users:<name>:ids, user:<id>:email) are read only by parameterized routes the selection rule excludes.
redis.verification: FLUSHALL is deliberately NOT used: the instance is shared, so flushing it would destroy other processes' state. The absence of the one region that matters is measured instead, and the replay reproduces every recorded body digest, which is the empirical confirmation.

initialization: docker exec trinket-mongo mongosh --quiet --eval 'db.getSiblingDB("test_baseline").dropDatabase()' -- executed OUT OF BAND, from outside the application process, before boot. The harness itself never calls dropDatabase and never requires test/helpers/db.js, so it cannot collide with the existing suite's database lifecycle. The name it drops is the harness's own forced disposable database and nothing else.

docker exec trinket-redis redis-cli KEYS 'snippets*' -- a READ, not a flush, confirming the one state-sensitive Redis region is absent (see redis.stateThatMatters). The shared instance is never flushed.

fingerprintAfterCapture.note: The fifteen collections are created by mongoose index building at boot. Only `sessions` holds documents — the server-side yar/catbox records for the capture's own requests, since app.js sets maxCookieSize: 0. `snippets` is 0 and `users` is back to 0 because the throwaway identity was removed. Redis finished at DBSIZE 0: the application never writes a snippets:* key on any corpus path, so trinketStore.byCategory's EXISTS check is false and findFeaturedTrinkets deterministically yields [].

datastoreState.featuredRegionDeterminismRule: For every GET /<lang> landing the featured region is fixed by construction: with snippets:<lang>:featured absent, byCategory returns null, namedTrinketList returns [], and trinket.index assigns data.trinkets = []. Any replay MUST start from the same explicitly initialized state — an empty snippets:*:featured keyspace and an empty `test` database — or the comparison is not a like-for-like one. Measurement additionally shows the region is not merely fixed but inert: see gates.stateSensitivityControls.seededFeaturedTrinket. NO structural normalization of the region is applied, and none is needed; the recorded digests are whole-document digests of the normalized body.
stateSensitiveEntries: authenticated GET /home — depends on throwawayUser.fullname and throwawayUser.ownedTrinkets, both pinned
datastoreState.stateInsensitiveEntries: all 58 unauthenticated entries and the other 6 authenticated entries — proven by the seeded-featured control, not assumed

metadata.capturedBy: test/baseline/capture.js, run inside the base-commit checkout described in metadata.captureCheckout. The harness that owns this artifact is the harness that produced it.
metadata.transport: real HTTP against server.info.uri — server.inject() is NEVER used
metadata.appUrlOriginNote: The origin lib/http/redirect.js absolutizes against, derived from config.app.url (config/default.yaml: protocol https, hostname trinket.dev, no port). Ten of the sixteen recorded redirects carry an absolute Location built from it, and every rendered page embeds it in markup, so the recorded digests are only meaningful against this origin. It is a PRECONDITION of every capture and every replay, not something either one adjusts: test/baseline/capture.js#originPrecondition compares the live origin with this value and reports UNABLE TO RUN (exit 2) with the remedy when they differ. Nothing is rebased -- an earlier revision rewrote each measured Location onto this origin before comparing, which would have let a build emitting the wrong configured origin replay clean. config/local.example.yaml (the file docs/setup.md tells a developer to copy to config/local.yaml, loaded last by node-config) declares http://localhost:3000 instead, so a developer checkout must drop that app.url block or export a matching NODE_CONFIG before replaying. The absolute-versus-relative split stays pinned by gates.absoluteRedirectCount and gates.relativeRedirectCount, and every Location is compared byte for byte.

throwawayUser.createdThrough: the application's own global User model, then logged in over real HTTP via POST /login
throwawayUser.isACaptureInput: Every field above is pinned because it is an INPUT to recorded values, not decoration. fullname is rendered into authenticated GET /home by lib/views/base.html:L124 as alt="Photo of {{ user.name }}" (lib/models/user.js:L33-L34 copies fullname into name on first save), so it determines that entry's bodyShape.sha256; measured directly, eight same-length candidates produced eight different digests and only "baseline capture" produces the recorded digest f7d1e5d3c27b175cfebf0a57431fd541d8a836c9e008e40884c475feb82972b0 at 18126 raw / 17206 normalized bytes. That digest is the FIRST-HOP value and it is the one recorded here: the intervening revision of this artifact recorded a207e0fc… at 18055 / 17135 because its redirect-resolution pass had consumed the post-login flash before this entry was measured, which is the defect requestPolicy.resolutionReading now makes structurally impossible. passwordLength and invalidPasswordSuffix determine the two POST /login request content-length values (73 = 54 + 19 and 81 = 54 + 19 + 8); the password itself is never rendered, so it affects no response field. ownedTrinkets determines the same /home digest through Trinket.findRecentByOwner -- see gates.stateSensitivityControls.throwawayUserOwnedTrinket.

metadata.cleanCheckoutNotes: Reproducing this capture on a clean checkout needs four things and no more: (1) `npm ci` against the base-commit lockfile — 642 packages, exit 0 on Node 22; (2) a reachable MongoDB on db.mongo.host/port -- the harness forces its own disposable database, metadata.database, and validates it before every write -- and a reachable Redis, since config/redis.js treats db.redis.enabled !== false as enabled; (3) a session cookie password of at least 32 characters, or app.js:L50-L66 calls process.exit(1); and (4) the datastore initialized to the state recorded in metadata.datastoreState and the throwaway identity created exactly as recorded in metadata.throwawayUser — both are inputs to recorded values, not setup trivia. `npm run build`, which supplies the buildArtifacts digests below, additionally FAILS on a clean checkout until public/components is hydrated from the public-components.tgz asset of release v1.1.0 (measured at exactly 166,464,007 bytes, Foundation 5.5.3); that tree is gitignored and must not be committed.
captureNotes: On `capturedBy` and regeneration: this revision was produced by test/baseline/capture.js itself, run inside a checkout of metadata.baseCommit, so the artifact and its owner can no longer drift. The procedure is the one the AAP specifies: boot through require('../../app.js') (which exports a Promise), read server.info, issue real HTTP requests with node:http and no Accept header, never follow the first hop, enforce a 15000 ms per-request timeout, and write both artifacts atomically. A plain run captures; `--dry-run` measures and diffs and writes nothing; there is NO --force. A write is refused unless HEAD is metadata.baseCommit AND no tracked file is modified, so post-migration or half-finished values cannot become the baseline, and `--adopt-base-commit` is the only way to move it -- which rewrites metadata.baseCommit so the change is on the record. Regeneration ownership is recorded separately in metadata.regenerationOwner, and a regenerating run must start from the datastore state recorded in metadata.datastoreState and the identity recorded in metadata.throwawayUser, or the state-sensitive entries named there will not reproduce.

NODE_ENV=test and NODE_CONFIG_PERSIST_ON_CHANGE=N were exported for the capture process. config/test.yaml (which sets app.start:false at L3) was NOT edited and config/local.yaml was NOT created: app.start:true, the bind host and port, the >=32-character session cookie password required by app.js:L50-L66 and the disposable database were all injected at runtime through the NODE_CONFIG environment variable recorded verbatim in nodeConfigOverride -- which is the override the run actually installed, read back out of the harness rather than transcribed.

nodeConfigOverride deliberately does NOT touch app.url, and neither the capture nor the replay rebases a measured value onto a different origin. config/app.config.js:L16-L17 computes config.url from app.url.{protocol,hostname,port}, which config/default.yaml:L30-L33 fixes at https + trinket.dev + (empty port), so config.url is https://trinket.dev independently of the bind host and port. Overriding it would rewrite every absolute Location in locationContract and destroy the absolute-versus-relative distinction this corpus exists to prove; rebasing a measured Location onto it would let a build that emits the wrong configured origin replay clean. A mismatch is therefore UNABLE TO RUN with a remedy -- see metadata.appUrlOriginNote.

The nodeConfigOverride session cookie password is a deliberate non-secret placeholder. It is a capture-time input, not a credential: it seals throwaway sessions for a throwaway user on a loopback port, and the sealed payload it produces is redacted everywhere in this artifact.

Reproducibility was measured, not assumed. Under the corrected policy the same base-commit tree was measured repeatedly -- separate processes, separate ports -- and produced ZERO differences in status, statusText, location, contentType, isApiRequest, header key sets, header values, Set-Cookie attribute sets, request header sets or body shape, under the single normalization recorded in normalizationContract.appliedInThisArtifact. The migrated working tree reproduces the same values: see gates.migratedReplay.

The corpus was additionally re-captured with @hapi/hapi 21.4.10, joi 18.2.3, accepts 1.3.8 and @hapi/inert 7.1.2 overlaid on the same unmodified source: ZERO differences across all 58 unauthenticated and all 7 authenticated entries. The corpus is therefore dependency-bump invariant, which is what makes it a valid parity baseline for a migrated server running the newer framework. See adjudications.

No application file was read-modified in producing this artifact, and nothing was added to test/baseline/ beyond the four sanctioned files. Both throwaway identities were created through the application's own global User model, exercised over real HTTP, and removed in a TERMINAL finally that attempts BOTH removals even when an earlier step threw and reports a failure to remove as a nonzero exit rather than swallowing it; a delete is refused outright if the document holding the harness email does not match the harness identity. dropDatabase and FLUSHALL are never called from inside the application process -- see metadata.datastoreState.initialization.

Replay: test/baseline/replay.js is the falsification tool. It boots the application the same way, re-derives the route-table canonicalization and both authoritative digests from the LIVE server, replays this corpus over real HTTP through capture.js's own helpers and normalization, re-measures the two build artifacts and the source-map count, and NEVER writes an artifact. Its exits distinguish the three outcomes: 0 parity, 1 a real difference, 2 unable to run (bad flags, a missing or malformed artifact, an origin that does not match this one, absent build evidence, a boot failure or a cleanup failure). Its detection power was mutation-proven rather than assumed: flipping one recorded status (GET /about 200 -> 201), corrupting one recorded canonical route row, and altering one recorded HTML body digest (authenticated GET /home) each produced exactly one reported difference and exit code 1, and each artifact was then restored byte-identically. test/lib/api/route-parity.js carries the same gates inside `npm test`, appended after the original nine in test/lib/api/index.js without reordering them.

On the two control experiments in gates.stateSensitivityControls: both were run in the same isolated environment against the same unmodified source, purely to establish which recorded fields are state-sensitive. Their seeded documents are NOT part of the recorded baseline -- every recorded value comes from the un-seeded run against the fingerprinted empty state.

The consuming hop's Location IS the measurement -- the destination the frozen assignment UI persisted -- so following it would stop measuring this contract and start measuring whatever page that destination renders, which depends on database state the flow does not own. The same rule that protects the authenticated section applies here: the legs pin a session cookie, and requestPolicy.resolutionReading never sends one. Previous wording of this key: Deliberately NOT followed for this section. The consuming hop's Location IS the measurement, and following it would stop measuring this contract and start measuring whatever page the destination resolves to, which depends on datastore state the assignment flow does not own. selectionRule.description: GET routes from the live route table whose path contains no parameter segment
selectionRule.rationale: Reproducible rather than hand-curated: the corpus is a pure function of the registered route table, so it cannot drift with reviewer taste and it re-derives identically on any checkout. Parameterless paths are exactly the set that can be requested without inventing fixture data. That is a fixture-independence property, NOT a datastore-independence property, and it must not be read as one: GET /python genuinely reads Redis and MongoDB through its findFeaturedTrinkets pre-handler. Replay determinism is therefore guaranteed by initializing and recording that state — see metadata.datastoreState — and the measured consequence of the read is recorded in gates.stateSensitivityControls.
selectionRule.compositionNote: The 11 language landings and 11 trailing-slash pages come from the config/routes.js language loop over the 11 trinketLangs declared in config/constants.js (python, python3, console, music, html, blocks, glowscript, java, glowscript-blocks, R, pygame). The 2 static pages are synthesized by routeParser.js:L742-L765 from lib/views/static/about.html and help.html. Note that /r and /R are distinct rows: /r is a parameterless alias with no pre-handlers, /R is the language landing for the (disabled) R type.

requestPolicy.acceptHeaderRationale: Derived from the 7x401 gate, not chosen. app.js:L159-L168 computes isApiRequest as path.startsWith("/api/") || accept.includes("application/json") || path.startsWith("/partials/"), and only takes the HTML error branch when !isApiRequest && wantsHtml. Twelve parameterless GETs require a session — seven under /api/ and five not (/account, /admin, /courses/new, /home, /welcome). With no Accept header the seven /api/ routes emit raw 401 and the five non-API routes emit h.redirect("/login").takeover(), which is the measured 7x401. With Accept: application/json every path becomes an API request and all twelve emit 401, i.e. 12 != 7. Sending no Accept header also matches test/helpers/flow.js createRequest, which sets only referer, and it is what makes accepts(request).types(["html","json"]) at routeParser.js:L325 return the first offered type "html", activating the success.html / fail.redirect branches.
requestPolicy.refererRationale: config.url on every request, matching test/helpers/flow.js:L414 request.set("referer", config.url) so the corpus is indistinguishable from the repository's own client.
requestPolicy.userAgentRationale: Pinned literally because routeParser.js:L29-L39 (isMobile) and L41-L52 (aceOff) sniff the User-Agent and their output reaches the templates. Replay MUST send this exact string. Measured effect of this value: isMobile false, aceOff false.
requestPolicy.followRedirectsRationale: The PRIMARY reading of every entry is the raw first hop and it is never followed: `status`, `location`, `headers`, `setCookie` and `bodyShape` are the immediate response, which is what test/helpers/flow.js and test/lib/api/login.js assert and what carries the absolute-versus-relative evidence in locationContract. config.url is https://trinket.dev, computed at config/app.config.js:L16-L17 from config/default.yaml:L30-L33 and independent of the bind host and port, and the redirect helper at lib/http/redirect.js absolutizes any leading-slash target to config.url + target, so most Location values carry the production origin. A SECOND, strictly additive reading resolves each UNAUTHENTICATED entry's chain to its terminal response, because that resolved reading is the one the Technical Specification's published 25/7/25/1 tally counts (§0.7.5); see resolutionReading for the two rules that make it provably unable to perturb the primary reading. The authenticated and assignment sections have ONE reading only and carry no redirectChain or resolved field.
requestPolicy.timeoutRationale: Mandatory. routeParser.js:L568-L570 is `if (result === undefined) { result = await responsePromise; }`, so a handler that neither returns a value nor calls request.success/request.fail waits forever. The timeout converts that into a recorded "timeout" outcome for one route instead of a hung run. No route in this corpus hit it.

measuredLengths.derivation: The serialized template is 54 bytes plus the password length, so 54 + 19 = 73 for the valid attempt and 54 + 19 + 8 = 81 for the invalid attempt, which appends metadata.throwawayUser.invalidPasswordSuffix. Replay must use a password of the recorded passwordLength and the recorded suffix to reproduce these two values; the password text itself is never rendered and affects no response field.

headersSent.notSentNote: Issued with node:http, which adds only Host and Connection beyond the headers listed above. No Accept and no Accept-Encoding is sent, so no response in this corpus is content-encoded and every content-length is the identity length.

resolutionReading.what: The ADDITIVE resolved reading: for each unauthenticated entry, the terminal response of its Location chain, recorded per entry as `redirectChain` (one row per hop) and `resolved` (status, contentType, bytes, kind, title, hops, stoppedBecause). It exists because the Technical Specification publishes the corpus outcome as 25x200 / 7x401 / 25x404 / 1x500, which is a REDIRECT-RESOLVED tally: the first-hop tally of the same 58 routes is {200:12, 302:16, 401:7, 404:22, 500:1}. Both readings are recorded and both are gated, because they answer different questions and neither replaces the other.
resolutionReading.runsAfter: the unauthenticated, authenticated and assignmentNext sections are ALL recorded
resolutionReading.whyThoseTwoRulesAreLoadBearing: An earlier revision of this artifact resolved the AUTHENTICATED chains too, with the pinned session cookie, interleaved with the primary capture. yar session storage is single-read, so those extra GETs consumed the post-login flash and changed a PRIMARY recorded value: authenticated GET /home was recorded at 18055 raw / 17135 normalized bytes (sha256 a207e0fc271ba246033db9fa4bdd7546c9eb98112ddb5ed800559912e77c368d) instead of the 18126 / 17206 (sha256 f7d1e5d3c27b175cfebf0a57431fd541d8a836c9e008e40884c475feb82972b0) the same base commit produces when nothing is followed with a cookie. The pass was 'additive' in name only. It is additive in fact now, for two structural reasons rather than by discipline: test/baseline/capture.js#followRedirectChain has NO parameter through which a cookie could be passed, and resolveUnauthenticated() is step 4 of captureCorpus() -- there is no recorded value left for it to move. Measured after the correction: the 58 unauthenticated entries and the 8 assignment entries are byte-identical to the pre-follow revision, and GET /home is back to 18126 / 17206.
resolutionReading.sameApplicationRule: A hop is followed when its Location is relative, or absolute with an origin EXACTLY equal to config.url (https://trinket.dev) or to the probe origin. Equality is computed with the non-throwing static URL.parse and compared on .origin, never as a string prefix: https://trinket.dev.evil.example/x and https://trinket.dev@evil.example/x both begin with the configured origin as a string, and a prefix test would have mapped either onto the local probe and requested it. Any other origin, a protocol-relative value and an unparseable value are recorded and NEVER requested, so the resolution cannot leave the process under test.
resolutionReading.loopGuard: a URL already visited in the same chain is recorded but not re-requested
resolutionReading.methodOnHops: Every followed hop is a GET, per RFC 9110 302 handling, which is also what a browser and `curl -L` do. The seed hop is the entry's own already-recorded first hop and is never re-issued, so the 42 non-redirecting entries cost no request at all.
resolutionReading.whyNotDerivedWithoutRequests: Resolving the chains arithmetically from the corpus itself -- following each recorded Location to the recorded entry for that path -- reproduces 56 of the 58 terminal statuses but yields {200:23, 302:2, 401:7, 404:25, 500:1}, because /change-email and /verify-email both redirect to /account/email, which the selection rule excludes (it is served by the parameterized route /account/{page}). A zero-request derivation therefore cannot reproduce the published tally, which is why the reading is a real cookie-less request pass rather than a calculation.

requestPolicy.originHandling: NEITHER the capture nor the replay overrides config.app.url, and no measured value is ever rewritten onto a different origin. An earlier revision did both -- it injected metadata.appUrlOrigin into a verify run and rebased each measured Location before comparing -- which would have let a build that emitted the WRONG configured origin replay clean, and the literal Location is exactly what R-5 requires be proven. A run whose live app.url origin differs from metadata.appUrlOrigin is UNABLE TO RUN (exit 2) and says so with the remedy: drop the app.url block from config/local.yaml, or export a matching NODE_CONFIG. Configuration mismatch is a precondition failure, never a normalization.

normalizationContract.description: The contract replay.js consumes. It names, on one side, the values that are genuinely volatile and may be neutralized before comparison and, on the other, the values that ARE the behavior under test and must be compared literally.
appliedInThisArtifact: The `date` response header is stored as "<normalized:date>" on every entry.
The Expires attribute value appended to the session cookie by app.js:L205-L240 is stored as "Expires=<normalized:expires>"; the PRESENCE of the attribute is contractual, the absolute date is not.

The iron-sealed cookie payload is stored as "Fe26.2*<REDACTED_IRON_SEAL_PAYLOAD>" wherever it appears — in Set-Cookie response headers AND in the Cookie request header that the authenticated entries replayed; the cookie name and the Fe26.2 prefix are preserved verbatim, because the prefix itself is contractual.
HTML bodies are stored as a normalized sha256 plus byte counts, title and structural markers — never verbatim. The normalization rules are listed under htmlBodyNormalization.
Un-normalized (raw) HTML digests are deliberately NOT stored: they were measured to differ between identical runs, so shipping them would manufacture false parity failures.
mayBeNormalized: the Connection, Keep-Alive and Transfer-Encoding response headers
ETag and Last-Modified on statically served assets
generated MongoDB ObjectIds, timestamps and ISO date strings inside bodies
the payload of the iron-sealed cookie value — everything after the Fe26.2 prefix
the Expires=<date> value appended by the cookie rewrite (presence is contractual, the date is not)
the ephemeral port inside any self-referential URL
mustNotBeNormalized: the cookie name `session` and the Fe26.2 prefix
the set of Set-Cookie attributes — Expires present only on cookie-declaring routes, SameSite=Lax always, Secure and SameSite=None never, Domain never
the Cache-Control, Pragma and Expires response headers, and X-Frame-Options
the literal Location value — absolute versus relative is the whole point
the set of body keys and the stable scalar values inside Boom payloads

htmlBodyNormalization.digest: sha256 of the UTF-8 body after the rules below, recorded per entry as bodyShape.sha256

lib/util/roles.js:L13 returns token + "+" + encrypted and ships it to the browser, which decrypts it at public/js/trinket-roles.js:L10-L11. The AES envelope carries a fresh OpenSSL salt per render. This was the LAST residual run-to-run difference, found by diffing raw authenticated GET /home bodies, and it is a preserved quirk (obfuscation, not security) rather than something to repair.
rules.enforcement: GATED. Substitution is NOT unconditional: test/baseline/capture.js#normalizeHtmlBody re-scans the body with ([0-9a-f]{32})\+(U2FsdGVkX1[A-Za-z0-9+/=]*) and passes every match through capture.js#assertRolesTokenStructure BEFORE this replacement is applied. That function verifies the four invariants in cryptoParityContract.invariants and THROWS on any violation rather than erasing it, so a build whose passphrase, envelope or block structure changed cannot hide behind this rule. Only the random bytes — the salt and the ciphertext they derive — are normalized away; the structure is asserted. Every verified match is tallied in capture.js#ROLES_TOKEN_OBSERVATIONS and printed by the harness. See cryptoParityContract and the adjudication "roles-token-structure-gated-not-erased".

rules.reason: any other OpenSSL "Salted__" envelope reaching the page.

volatilityProof.note: Two full capture runs in separate processes against separate ports were compared field by field under exactly the rules above and produced zero differences. Every normalization listed was justified by an observed difference; none was added speculatively.

normalizationContract.prohibition: Do NOT normalize away a difference in order to make a replay diff pass. Every rule above exists because a value was measured to be volatile between two identical runs. If a replay difference is real, it is an application-code defect and must be reported as one.

cryptoParityContract.purpose: The roles token is the one value in this corpus that is BOTH volatile between identical runs and a client-visible cryptographic contract, so normalizing it is unavoidable and normalizing it carelessly is dangerous. This block records the measured structure that must hold, so the normalization can neutralize the random bytes without also concealing a change of passphrase, key derivation, cipher mode or padding that would break the frozen browser decryptor.
cryptoParityContract.producerSource: var token = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex'); var encrypted = CryptoJS.AES.encrypt(obj, token).toString(); return token + '+' + encrypted;
cryptoParityContract.consumerSource: var v = $('#roles').val().split('+'); var t = v[0]; var e = v.slice(1).join('+'); var d = CryptoJS.AES.decrypt(e, t); roles = JSON.parse(CryptoJS.enc.Utf8.stringify(d));
cryptoParityContract.shippedVia: the nunjucks `encrypt` filter at lib/util/nunjucks.js:L58-L60, into the value of #roles
cryptoParityContract.wireFormat: <32 lowercase hex characters> + "+" + <base64 OpenSSL "Salted__" AES envelope>
invariants: the passphrase half matches /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/ — 16 random bytes hex-encoded, so exactly 32 lowercase hex characters and never more or fewer
the ciphertext half begins with the base64 prefix U2FsdGVkX1, which is the OpenSSL envelope marker
the base64 length is a whole number of 4-character quanta
the first 8 raw bytes decode to the literal ASCII magic "Salted__", and the raw length is a whole number of 16-byte AES blocks

lengthRelation.rawBytesExplanation: an 8-byte "Salted__" magic plus an 8-byte salt, followed by AES-CBC ciphertext padded with PKCS#7, which always appends at least one byte and therefore a whole extra block when the plaintext length is already a multiple of 16.
lengthRelation.consequence: Because the length is a deterministic function of the plaintext length, it is safe to ASSERT rather than normalize: a same-length regression is caught by the round trip, and a different-length regression is caught by the length checks.

observedInThisCorpus.note: Exactly one entry in the whole corpus carries a roles token, which is consistent with the normalization rule’s own history: it was added last, after diffing raw authenticated GET /home bodies between two runs. 464 raw bytes is 16 + 28*16 and 620 is ceil(464/3)*4, both exactly as the length relation predicts.

cryptoParityContract.roundTrip: ASSERTED, not assumed. test/lib/api/route-parity.js decrypts a freshly produced token with the same crypto-js primitives and the same split-and-join the browser uses — split('+'), v[0] as the passphrase, v.slice(1).join('+') as the ciphertext, CryptoJS.AES.decrypt, CryptoJS.enc.Utf8.stringify — and compares the parsed result against the original object. This is what catches a same-length key-derivation, key or cipher change, which the structural checks alone could not see.
cryptoParityContract.enforcement: Three layers, all reproducible from committed code: (1) capture.js#assertRolesTokenStructure gates every substitution and throws on violation; (2) test/lib/api/route-parity.js asserts the five invariants, the length relation and the browser round trip, and asserts that four near-miss tokens which match the normalization pattern are REJECTED rather than normalized -- against its own statement of the contract rather than by calling capture.js's gate, because that suite may not couple itself to the harness it corroborates (review finding F-API-1), which also makes a divergence between the two statements a failure rather than a shared blind spot; (3) replay.js reports the per-run token observations alongside the diff.
cryptoParityContract.preservedQuirk: The AES passphrase is shipped to the browser next to the ciphertext and split apart client-side. That is obfuscation, not security, and it is a PRESERVED quirk under R-4 — documented in docs/PRESERVED-QUIRKS.md, never repaired. This contract exists to keep the obfuscation byte-compatible, not to make it secure.

gates.authority: The Technical Specification is the authoritative parity anchor for this corpus. gates.documentedDistribution is the gate and it is REPRODUCED: measuring the corpus and then resolving each unauthenticated entry's Location chain back onto the same application -- cookie-less, and only after every primary reading is already recorded (requestPolicy.resolutionReading) -- yields exactly 25x200, 7x401, 25x404 and 1x500. Nothing in this artifact supersedes the Specification; where the two appeared to conflict, the artifact was corrected, not the Specification. The first-hop reading is retained beside it as subordinate evidence, and every value in both readings is recomputed from the live server by test/baseline/replay.js on every run.
gates.distributionAuthorityNote: gates.measuredDistribution is the RESOLVED reading -- the terminal status of every recorded Location chain, measured with no cookie on any hop and strictly after the whole primary corpus is recorded -- and it equals gates.documentedDistribution. It is re-derived from the live server on every run by test/baseline/replay.js, so it is a mechanical regression gate as well as the reproduction of the documented figure. It does not stand in for the Specification and it supersedes nothing.
gates.firstHopStatusDistributionNote: Subordinate evidence, not the gate. This is the immediate response before any hop is followed, and it is byte-identical to the previous revision of this artifact. It is retained because the 16x302 class carries the absolute-versus-relative Location evidence in locationContract and the takeover mechanics in gates.takeoverRedirectsToLogin.
gates.resolvedStatusDistributionNote: Identical by construction to gates.measuredDistribution, under the name test/baseline/replay.js uses when it compares the resolved reading explicitly. Both are asserted on every run.
gates.distributionNote: Measurement settles it, and it settles it IN FAVOUR of the documented tally. The documented figure omits the 3xx class because it reports the RESOLVED status of every route; the previous revision of this artifact reported the unfollowed first hop, which is the whole of the apparent conflict. See the adjudication "documented-distribution-is-the-authoritative-gate" for the per-status, per-route derivation (12 + 13 = 25 x 200 and 22 + 3 = 25 x 404). Nothing was changed to make the documented figures true.
gates.redirectResolutionNote: Thirteen of the sixteen 3xx routes resolve to 200 and three resolve to 404. The three 404s are the language aliases /r -> /R, /vpython -> /glowscript and /webvpython -> /glowscript, whose targets are themselves feature-flag 404s, so they join the 404 class. 12 + 13 = 25 x 200 and 22 + 3 = 25 x 404, which is how the documented distribution is arrived at.

gates.xFrameOptionsNote: Present on exactly these paths among the 58, all of them 200 responses. config.app.xframeDeny actually declares FIVE entries (/, /login, /signup, /contact, /educators); /contact and /educators are not registered routes at all, so they cannot appear. See the adjudication "xframe-deny-declares-five-paths".

Report it as a conversion defect; do NOT adjust this corpus. Under the corrected request policy the 500 is measured on the first and only hop of each of those two entries; nothing about the quirk depends on how redirects are treated.

cookieContract.name: session
cookieContract.sealPrefixNote: The raw value begins "Fe26.2**<mac>*<salt>*..." — a double asterisk, since the second field is empty. app.js sets maxCookieSize: 0, so the session itself lives server-side in the `sessions` catbox cache (CatboxMongoose.Engine) and the cookie carries only the sealed id.
cookieContract.ttlNote: From app.js, which builds the yar options object itself with cache.expiresIn = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000. This OVERRIDES config/default.yaml's expiresIn: 2147483647, because only password, isSecure and name are read from config.
cookieContract.appendedAttributesNote: The rewrite at app.js:L205-L240 appends "; Expires=<nextYear UTC>" and, only when cookieIsSecure is true, "; SameSite=None; Secure". config/default.yaml sets cookieOptions.isSecure: false, so cookieIsSecure === false and ONLY Expires is appended. The rewrite is further gated on request.cookie — set by routeParser.js:L354-L356 only when the route declares cookie:true — and on typeof request.response._header === "function", and it matches only values whose indexOf(sessionName) === 0.
cookieContract.domainNote: config/default.yaml declares cookieOptions.domain: .trinket.dev, but app.js never passes domain to yar, so no Domain attribute is ever emitted. Measured, not inferred.
cookieContract.cookieDeclaringRoutesNote: SIX routes declare cookie:true, not five. This list previously omitted POST /api/users, which is the second of the two declarations in config/api_routes.js and therefore the easiest to miss. The six are enumerated here with their declaration sites, in declaration order, and the count was re-measured by grepping cookie:true across both route files at HEAD and at the base commit 2f8712a — 4 in config/routes.js plus 2 in config/api_routes.js in BOTH trees, so the set is unchanged by the migration.

cookieRouteParity.purpose: Set-Cookie / Expires parity coverage for POST /api/users, the route added to cookieDeclaringRoutes above. It cannot be represented as a corpus entry without violating selectionRule (the unauthenticated corpus is parameterless GET routes only, and its 58-row count is a gate), so its measurement is recorded here instead. Measured over real HTTP against a genuinely bound server — server.inject was not used — under NODE_ENV=test with no config/local.yaml present and the same nodeConfigOverride recorded in metadata, using a throwaway identity that was removed in a finally block.
cookieRouteParity.expiresValueShape: nextYear UTC — measured as a valid UTC date string whose getUTCFullYear() equals the current year plus one, matching the rewrite at app.js:L205-L240.
cookieRouteParity.equivalenceToAlreadyCoveredCookieRoute: Its attribute list is IDENTICAL to POST /login's, which the authenticated section of this corpus already covers, so the two cookie-declaring code paths are measured to agree.
cookieRouteParity.contrastWithOrdinaryRoute: GET /signup, which does not declare cookie:true, emitted ["HttpOnly","SameSite","Path"] with NO Expires in the same run — confirming that Expires is appended only for cookie-declaring routes and that measuredAttributesOrdinaryRoute above is reproducible.

cookieContract.noSetCookieNote: A Set-Cookie appears only where the request actually touched the yar session. The two synthesized static pages never touch it (routeParser.js:L742-L765), and the Boom paths that short-circuit before the handler never reach it either.
cookieContract.doNotOverride: Do NOT override cookieOptions.isSecure in a capture or replay NODE_CONFIG: that would append "; SameSite=None; Secure" and change an observable header.

The destination is now simply not persisted, which leaves the session exactly as it is for a visitor who supplied no `next` at all, so the declared success.redirect '/home' answers.
The scheme-relative form of the same hole: a browser resolves it against the current scheme and leaves the origin.
The signup half of the same hole; the declared success.redirect '/welcome' answers instead.

errorMappingContract.messageComparisonRule: Compare every 4xx message string byte for byte — it is client-visible. Treat 5xx message strings as message-invariant: hapi replaces them with the fixed string above, so internal error text cannot be observed and must not be asserted.
errorMappingContract.unauthorizedMessagesNote: Constructed at app.js:L251/L264/L269/L277 as h.unauthenticated(Boom.unauthorized(msg), {credentials:{}}). Every one of the seven 401 bodies in this corpus carries "Not logged in" — the no-session branch. The other three require a session whose user is missing, disabled, or whose lookup threw, and are not reachable from an unauthenticated parameterless GET.
errorMappingContract.requestFailNote: routeParser.js:L482-L514: request.fail redirects only when responseType === "html" && fail.redirect, then renders only when responseType === "html" && fail.html && !JSON_EXT.test(pathname); OTHERWISE it falls through to h.response(json), which is HTTP 200 with a JSON body. request.success is symmetric at L474-L478. That is why GET /auth/google answers 200 rather than a 4xx, and it also means a joi validation failure (L537-L540 calls request.fail(request.payload, ...)) can surface as a 200 carrying {flash: {validation: {...}}} whenever the route declares neither fail.redirect nor fail.html.
errorMappingContract.validationFailureSurfaces: Measured in this corpus as an absolute 302 on GET /reset-pass, GET /change-email and GET /verify-email, because each declares a fail.redirect. A rejected input is therefore never a 4xx on these routes — preserving that is what "validation outcomes unchanged" means here.
errorMappingContract.renderedErrorPagesHeaderNote: MEASURED REFINEMENT. The rendered branches at app.js:L170-L176 all `return` before the header block at app.js:L182-L190, so the application's Cache-Control string, Pragma, Expires and X-Frame-Options are absent from 404.html and 50x.html responses and from the takeover redirect to /login. They are NOT header-free, however: hapi's own default Cache-Control: no-cache is present. Assert the absence of the application string and of Pragma/Expires/X-Frame-Options, not the absence of Cache-Control.
errorMappingContract.applicationCacheControl: private, s-maxage=0, max-age=0, no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate
errorMappingContract.boomCacheControlNote: MEASURED REFINEMENT. app.js assigns the application Cache-Control string to response.output.headers on Boom responses, but hapi's response marshalling applies the route cache policy afterwards, so every Boom response in this corpus shows Cache-Control: no-cache while Pragma: no-cache and Expires: 0 do survive. Preserved as measured.
errorMappingContract.isApiRequestSplit: Recorded per entry as isApiRequest, computed exactly as app.js:L160-L162 does: path starts with /api/, or the Accept header includes application/json, or the path starts with /partials/. It decides whether a Boom error emerges as raw JSON or as a rendered HTML error page, and it is the reason GET /api/users/assets yields Boom JSON rather than 50x.html.
errorMappingContract.boomMessageVisibilityByBranch: On the API branch the Boom message is on the wire (the seven 401s carry "Not logged in", the two /api/ 404s carry hapi's default "Not Found"). On the HTML branch the rendered page REPLACES the payload, so Boom.notFound("This trinket type is not available") from lib/util/helpers.js is never observable — only the 404.html body is.
errorMappingContract.thrownVersusReturned: QUALIFIED — the equivalence is a property of @hapi/hapi ALONE, and it does NOT survive lib/util/routeParser.js's catch. Bare hapi 21.4.10 is symmetric: a handler that throws Boom.notFound('nf-msg') and one that returns it both produce 404 with message "nf-msg", and the same holds for Boom.forbidden at 403. But every routed handler in this application runs inside routeParser.js's try/catch (L143 open, L229 catch, L238 `return ErrorMap.toResponse(err)`), and lib/http/errorMap.js:L41-L57 contains NO isBoom test — it unconditionally returns Boom.badImplementation(err.message || String(err)) for ANY truthy caught value, Boom included. So inside a routed handler a THROWN 4xx Boom is swallowed and remapped to a scrubbed 500, while a RETURNED 4xx Boom passes through routeParser's try block untouched and reaches hapi with its status and message intact. The two forms are therefore NOT interchangeable at 4xx. They remain equivalent at 5xx, because remapping a 500 to a 500 is a no-op and hapi scrubs both messages identically.

thrownVersusReturnedMeasured.measurement: Real HTTP against a live @hapi/hapi 21.4.10 server (server.inject not used), exercising the repository's own unmodified lib/http/errorMap.js module. Group B routes are bare hapi; Group A routes are wrapped in the exact try/catch + ErrorMap.toResponse shape routeParser.js uses.

insideRouteParserCatch.throw Boom.notFound('nf-msg'): 500  message="An internal server error occurred"  <-- REMAPPED
insideRouteParserCatch.throw Boom.forbidden('fb-msg'): 500  message="An internal server error occurred"  <-- REMAPPED

thrownVersusReturnedMeasured.consequenceForConversion: The 64 reply(Boom.x()) sites are safe in the RETURN form, which is the form the shim itself used and the form errorMap.js deliberately preserves. Converting any of them to `throw` would silently collapse a 4xx into a 500 wherever the Boom is raised inside the handler body. This is why the conversion standardised on returning, and why the 41 pre-existing `throw Boom.*` sites in lib/controllers/course.js — which reference an undeclared `Boom` identifier and therefore raise a ReferenceError before any Boom is constructed — already answered a scrubbed 500 at the base commit and still do.
thrownVersusReturnedMeasured.corpusScope: The corpus asserts the wire result, not the syntax that produced it, so it constrains the migrated server correctly either way; this note exists so the equivalence is not mistaken for a licence to swap the two forms.

adjudications.ambiguity: Which Accept header should the corpus send? The choice silently changes how many routes answer 401.
adjudications.evidence: app.js:L159-L168 makes isApiRequest true for ANY path when the Accept header includes application/json. Twelve parameterless GETs require a session: seven under /api/ and five not. Measured with no Accept header: exactly seven 401s and five takeover redirects to /login. With Accept: application/json all twelve would be 401.
adjudications.resolution: Send NO Accept header at all, matching test/helpers/flow.js createRequest, which sets only referer. Recorded as requestPolicy.acceptHeader = null. This also makes accepts(request).types(["html","json"]) return "html", which is what activates the success.html and fail.redirect branches inside the shim.

adjudications.ambiguity: Should the capture follow 3xx responses? The Technical Specification 0.7.5 publishes the corpus outcome as 25x200 / 7x401 / 25x404 / 1x500, which only reconciles with a redirect-RESOLVED reading -- the first hop of the same 58 routes is {200:12, 302:16, 401:7, 404:22, 500:1} -- while a parity corpus must record the raw wire contract of each route and must not perturb what it measures. An intervening revision resolved every chain INCLUDING the authenticated ones, with the pinned session cookie, interleaved with the primary capture.
adjudications.evidence: Measured, twice. (1) A cookie-less resolution pass changes nothing it measures: the 58 unauthenticated entries are byte-identical across the revision that followed nothing and the revision that follows cookie-lessly -- zero differences over requestHeaders, status, statusText, headers, contentType, setCookie, setCookieAttributes, location, isApiRequest and bodyShape. (2) A COOKIE-BEARING pass does perturb: with the authenticated chains followed, authenticated GET /home was recorded at 18055 raw / 17135 normalized bytes (sha256 a207e0fc…) instead of 18126 / 17206 (sha256 f7d1e5d3…), because yar session storage is single-read and the followed hop consumed the post-login flash. (3) Resolving the chains arithmetically from the corpus instead of over HTTP reproduces 56 of 58 terminal statuses and yields {200:23, 302:2, 401:7, 404:25, 500:1}, because /change-email and /verify-email redirect to /account/email, which the selection rule excludes.
adjudications.resolution: BOTH readings are recorded, and the resolved one is bounded by the two rules in requestPolicy.resolutionReading: it never sends a cookie, and it runs only after every primary reading in all three sections is already recorded. It applies to the unauthenticated section only; the authenticated and assignment sections are first-hop only and carry no resolution fields. The first hop remains the compared wire contract -- raw status and literal Location -- and the resolved reading reproduces the Specification's published tally exactly, so neither the Specification (R-6) nor the prohibition on perturbing measured behavior (R-4) is traded away. capture.js#followRedirectChain has no parameter through which a cookie could be passed, so the defect cannot recur by inattention.
adjudications.priorEvidenceRetained: config.url is https://trinket.dev and routeParser.js:L713-L717 absolutizes leading-slash targets to config.url + target, so ten of the sixteen measured 3xx responses point off-host at the production domain. test/helpers/flow.js drives supertest with redirect following disabled, which is why test/lib/api/login.js asserts a raw 302.

adjudications.ambiguity: The existing technical specification implies reply.redirect works, which would make authenticated GET /login and GET /signup 302 to /home and /welcome.
adjudications.evidence: Measured with a real session cookie obtained by logging in over real HTTP: BOTH return 500 and render 50x.html (title "Something went wrong", byte-identical bodies), while unauthenticated they return 200. Mechanism traced end to end: the synthetic reply at routeParser.js:L360 is a BARE FUNCTION and its chainable builder (L375-L405) exposes redirect only on the object returned by CALLING reply(data), so the Hapi-16 property-form calls reply.redirect("/home") at lib/controllers/pages.js:L17 and reply.redirect("/welcome") at L27 raise TypeError; the single catch-all at routeParser.js:L578-L589 converts it to Boom.badImplementation; app.js:L175 renders 50x.html with the original status.
adjudications.resolution: Baseline wins: the 500 is the contract and is preserved. Converting these two calls to h.redirect(...) would silently "fix" them into 302s — a prohibited behavior change on a login page. This corpus is what catches that: if either route answers 302 after the migration, lib/controllers/pages.js was converted wrongly. Report it; do not adjust the corpus.

adjudications.ambiguity: The folder brief states the pre-existing 500 at GET /api/users/assets renders 50x.html.
adjudications.evidence: Measured content-type application/json, 96 bytes, body {"statusCode":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"An internal server error occurred"}. The path begins with /api/, so isApiRequest is true at app.js:L160-L162 and the HTML branch is skipped entirely. Root cause: config/api_routes.js:L1228 declares validate.query.type = Joi.string().optional() with no auth:"session", and lib/controllers/users.js:L466 calls request.query.type.toLowerCase() on the absent value. Also verified: lib/util/helpers.js exports no assetsEnabled pre-handler, so config/default.yaml features.assets:false does not gate this route — the handler is genuinely reached.
adjudications.resolution: The brief is corrected: Boom JSON, not a rendered page. The 500 itself is a preserved pre-existing condition (AAP quirk I14) and is reproduced, not repaired.

adjudications.ambiguity: Are the language 404s a routing gap or intended behavior, and should the contradictory comment in lib/util/features.js be fixed?
adjudications.evidence: config/default.yaml enables only features.trinkets.python; the other ten of the eleven trinketLangs are false. helpers.trinketTypeEnabled (lib/util/helpers.js:L211-L236) derives urlLang from the first path segment, adopts it only when features.isKnownTrinketType(urlLang) is true, and returns reply(Boom.notFound("This trinket type is not available")) when features.isTrinketTypeEnabled(lang) is false. Inside lib/util/features.js, isTrinketTypeEnabled carries the comment "Check if explicitly set; default to true if not specified" and then, for an unrecognised type, "Unknown types default to disabled for safety" followed by `return false` — the comment is directly contradicted by the code beneath it. isKnownTrinketType is a bare hasOwnProperty, which is the asymmetry that lets the two predicates disagree. Measured: exactly 20 rendered 404.html responses, the ten disabled languages times the two parameterless language routes.
adjudications.resolution: Intended behavior at baseline and preserved verbatim — the flags, the asymmetry and the contradictory comment all stay. Note that the Boom message is NOT observable on these routes: the rendered 404.html replaces the payload.

adjudications.ambiguity: Are Location values absolute or relative? Twenty-two flow.lastRedirect.pathname assertions and the URL-parsing base-argument decision in test/helpers/flow.js depend on the answer.
adjudications.evidence: All three patterns genuinely occur and are recorded with literal values in locationContract: ABSOLUTE from declarative success/fail redirects, which pass through the absolutizer at routeParser.js:L704-L723 (measured https://trinket.dev/home, /login, /, /python, /signup, /forgot-pass, /account/email, /glowscript, /R); RELATIVE from the synthetic builder's redirect at routeParser.js:L376-L380, which calls h.redirect(url) with no absolutization (measured /account/profile and /); and RELATIVE from the lifecycle at app.js:L170, h.redirect("/login").takeover() (measured /login on all five non-API session routes).
adjudications.resolution: Both forms are contractual and neither may be normalized. Any URL parsing of a Location value must tolerate a relative input, which is exactly why a base argument is required.

adjudications.ambiguity: The folder brief states the app.js rewrite appends both "; Expires=<nextYear UTC>" and "; SameSite=None; Secure".
adjudications.evidence: app.js:L203 computes cookieIsSecure = cookieOptions.isSecure !== false and config/default.yaml sets isSecure: false, so cookieIsSecure is false. Measured Set-Cookie on the cookie-declaring GET /logout: attributes [HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Expires] with SameSite=Lax; on an ordinary route such as GET /: [HttpOnly, SameSite, Path] with NO Expires, because the rewrite is gated on request.cookie. No Secure and no SameSite=None appears anywhere; no Domain appears anywhere, despite config/default.yaml declaring cookieOptions.domain.
adjudications.resolution: The brief is corrected. Only Expires is appended under this configuration, and only on cookie-declaring routes. Recorded in cookieContract with the effective isSecure so the assertion is interpretable. Do not override cookieOptions.isSecure in a capture or replay: that would change an observable header.

adjudications.ambiguity: Why do several routes answer 200 where a 4xx would be expected?
adjudications.evidence: routeParser.js:L482-L514 shows request.fail falling through to h.response(json) whenever the route declares neither fail.redirect (on the html branch) nor fail.html. Measured: GET /auth/google returns 200 application/json with keys ["flash","message"] and message "Google OAuth is not configured. Please set up Google OAuth credentials.", because config/default.yaml leaves app.auth.google.clientID empty and the route declares no fail block.
adjudications.resolution: Preserved and documented as a mapping, not a bug. errorMappingContract.requestFailWithoutRedirectOrHtmlYields records the value 200 so replay.js compares the right thing.

The only two *.css.map files anywhere under public/ are vendored inside public/components/foundation/css/ and arrive with the release tarball.

adjudications.ambiguity: An earlier revision of this artifact could not reproduce the Technical Specification 0.7.5 tally of 25x200, 7x401, 25x404 and 1x500 and declared its own measurement the contract instead, setting distributionMatchesDocumented to false.
adjudications.evidence: The deviation was traced to a single undocumented capture choice rather than to any application behaviour: requestPolicy.followRedirects was false. Sixteen of the 58 routes answer 3xx, a class the documented tally omits, and resolving them reconstructs the documented figure precisely -- thirteen resolve to 200 (12 + 13 = 25) and three resolve to 404 (22 + 3 = 25), while the 7x401 and the single 500 at GET /api/users/assets were never in dispute. Re-measured on the true base commit 2f8712a: a pristine `git archive` tree with that commit's own 642-package lockfile installed (@hapi/hapi 20.3.0, joi 17.13.3, marked 0.3.2, accepts 1.1.4, mongoose 6.13.9), 233 route rows, 58 corpus paths, over real HTTP. Every first-hop status and Location matched the previous revision exactly, so the two captures agree on what the server does and differ only on how far the client was followed.
adjudications.resolution: The AAP figure stands as the authoritative gate. gates.documentedDistribution is unchanged, gates.measuredDistribution now equals it, and gates.distributionMatchesDocumented is true. This artifact no longer supersedes the AAP: where the two appeared to conflict, the artifact was wrong about its own request policy, not the specification wrong about the application.
adjudications.priorEvidenceRetained: Measured over real HTTP: {"200":12,"302":16,"401":7,"404":22,"500":1}. The 7x401 and the single 500 at GET /api/users/assets match exactly. The deviation is entirely accounted for: (a) sixteen routes are 3xx, a class the documented tally omits — five non-API session routes take the app.js:L170 takeover redirect to /login; four aliases (/r, /skulpt, /vpython, /webvpython) carry success.redirect and NO pre array, so no feature-flag pre-handler can run; GET /logout carries a top-level redirect; GET /python/ is the language loop's trailing-slash redirect; GET /auth/google/callback uses fail.redirect; and GET /reset-pass, GET /change-email and GET /verify-email fail a required-query validation into a fail.redirect. (b) 404s measure 22, not 25: the 20 feature-flag language pages plus two Boom-JSON 404s at /api/trinkets/active and /api/trinkets/popular, whose cause is helpers.validLang deriving urlLang "api/trinkets/active" and finding it absent from Trinket.schema.path("lang").enumValues. (c) 200s measure 12, not 25, because thirteen of the documented 200s are in fact the 3xx above and two of the presumed language 200s are 404s.

adjudications.ambiguity: Which commit is "the base commit" for a corpus produced inside a batch whose earlier workers have already committed? An earlier revision of the sibling test/baseline/route-table.json recorded the dependency-manifest commit rather than the pre-run commit, so the two artifacts disagreed about their own denominator.
adjudications.evidence: The pre-run commit is 2f8712a112db46f923918c4507c75abc732d83d0. The next commit, cd9838994947ad91e02c1680341e2592b92a10cd, changes ONLY package.json and package-lock.json (git diff --name-status confirms two files), and sha256 comparison shows app.js, lib/util/routeParser.js, lib/controllers/pages.js, lib/controllers/users.js, lib/util/helpers.js, lib/util/features.js, config/routes.js, config/api_routes.js, config/default.yaml, config/constants.js and config/test.yaml byte-identical between the two. The commit after that modifies app.js and deletes lib/auth/passport.js, so it is not a baseline at all.

Since the application source is byte-identical to cd98389, this corpus and the sibling route-table.json describe the same code, and selectionRule.crossCheckedAgainstLiveTable records that the parameterless-GET set derived from that artifact equals the set derived from the live table. adjudications.ambiguity: A corpus captured on hapi 20.3.0 / joi 17.13.3 might diverge from a hapi 21 / joi 18 replay for reasons that belong to the dependency bump rather than to the code migration, which would make every such difference ambiguous.
adjudications.evidence: The entire capture was re-run with @hapi/hapi 21.4.10, joi 18.2.3, accepts 1.3.8 and @hapi/inert 7.1.2 overlaid on the SAME unmodified base source: ZERO differences across all 58 unauthenticated and all 7 authenticated entries in status, statusText, location, content-type, isApiRequest, header key sets, header values, Set-Cookie attribute sets and body shape.
adjudications.resolution: The ambiguity is removed by measurement rather than by argument: any difference a replay finds against the migrated server is attributable to the code migration, not to the framework or validator bump. Recorded in gates.dependencyBumpCrossCheck. Scope note: the overlaid run is a SUPPLEMENTAL cross-check, never the denominator. Every value recorded in this artifact comes from the pristine base-lockfile install described in metadata.captureCheckout.

adjudications.ambiguity: The folder brief states config/default.yaml app.xframeDeny lists exactly three paths.
adjudications.evidence: It lists FIVE: /, /login, /signup, /contact and /educators. /contact and /educators are not registered routes at all, so they cannot appear in any response. Measured among the 58: X-Frame-Options: deny on exactly /, /login and /signup, all 200s (and also on POST /login, which is a non-Boom response on a listed path).
adjudications.resolution: The observable claim stands and is asserted as measured; the config figure in the brief is corrected here. Nothing in config/default.yaml was touched.

adjudications.ambiguity: The folder brief states rendered 404.html and 50x.html responses carry no Cache-Control at all.
adjudications.evidence: Measured header key set on a rendered 404: cache-control, connection, content-length, content-type, date, keep-alive, vary — with cache-control: no-cache, hapi's default. Pragma, Expires and X-Frame-Options are genuinely absent, because app.js:L170-L176 returns before the header block at L182-L190. Separately, Boom responses that DO reach that block still show cache-control: no-cache, because hapi's marshalling applies the route cache policy after the extension assigns the application string to response.output.headers; Pragma: no-cache and Expires: 0 survive there.
adjudications.resolution: Assert the absence of the application Cache-Control string and of Pragma/Expires/X-Frame-Options — not the absence of the header itself. Both refinements are recorded in errorMappingContract and preserved as measured.

adjudications.ambiguity: Two /api/ routes answer 404 for no documented reason, which could be mistaken for a routing gap or for a feature flag.
adjudications.evidence: GET /api/trinkets/active and GET /api/trinkets/popular inherit auth mode=try and carry pre [helpers.trinketTypeEnabled, helpers.validLang]. trinketTypeEnabled passes because isKnownTrinketType("api") is false, so no lang is adopted. validLang then strips the leading and trailing slash to get urlLang from the request path itself — "api/trinkets/active" for the first route and "api/trinkets/popular" for the second — and, finding neither in Trinket.schema.path("lang").enumValues, returns Boom.notFound() with no message. Because the path is under /api/ the Boom is delivered as JSON with hapi's default message "Not Found".
adjudications.resolution: Recorded as measured and preserved. These are the two 404s that make the measured 404 tally 22 rather than the 20 that the feature flags alone explain, and they are counted separately in gates.boomJsonFourOhFours.

adjudications.ambiguity: Authenticated GET /home did not reproduce byte for byte between runs even after ObjectId, ISO-date and cache-prefix normalization, which could have been read as nondeterministic rendering.
adjudications.evidence: Diffing the two raw bodies isolated a single differing line: the hidden roles input, whose value is lib/util/roles.js:L13's token + "+" + AES envelope. The envelope carries a fresh OpenSSL salt on every render. Nothing else in the document differed.
adjudications.resolution: Neutralize exactly that value in the HTML normalization and leave the mechanism alone. Shipping the client the key it needs to decrypt the payload is obfuscation rather than security, and repairing it is out of scope; the corpus records the volatility and preserves the behavior.

adjudications.ambiguity: The roles-token normalization rule replaced the passphrase AND the whole OpenSSL envelope with the single literal <ROLES_TOKEN>. A regression that kept the same envelope length but changed the key derivation, the key or the cipher would therefore compare equal on replay while breaking the frozen browser decryptor at public/js/trinket-roles.js. The obvious remedy — make the replacement encode the measured lengths — was considered and rejected.
adjudications.evidence: Measured: exactly ONE corpus body carries a roles token (authenticated GET /home; hexLength 32, base64Length 620, rawByteLength 464). Changing the replacement string would therefore change that entry’s recorded bodyShape.sha256 and normalizedBytes — base-commit measurements that cannot be legitimately re-derived here, because commit 2f8712a cannot boot in this environment at all: its lib/util/routeParser.js requires `tab` and `optimist`, which the migrated lockfile no longer installs. Rewriting a base-commit digest from the migrated tree would replace evidence with assertion and would violate this artifact’s own prohibition.
adjudications.resolution: The substitution output is left byte-identical, so every recorded digest remains a genuine base-commit measurement, and the protection is added where it costs nothing: the rule is now GATED. test/baseline/capture.js#assertRolesTokenStructure verifies the four cryptoParityContract invariants for EVERY match before the substitution runs and throws rather than erasing, and test/lib/api/route-parity.js independently asserts the same invariants, the deterministic length relation and a real browser-compatible CryptoJS round trip — which is the check that catches a same-length key or cipher change. Four near-miss tokens that match the normalization pattern but violate the contract are asserted to be REJECTED. Nothing is normalized away in order to make a diff pass.

adjudications.ambiguity: Is a parameterless-GET corpus independent of persisted state? An earlier revision of selectionRule.rationale asserted that it is, which would make an un-initialized, un-fingerprinted datastore harmless — and would make any replay difference on GET /python unattributable.
adjudications.evidence: The assertion is false as stated. config/routes.js:L551-L570 gives every GET /<lang> landing pre [helpers.trinketTypeEnabled, {method: helpers.findFeaturedTrinkets, assign: featuredTrinkets}]; lib/util/helpers.js findFeaturedTrinkets calls internals.namedTrinketList(lang, "featured"), which calls trinketStore.byCategory — a Redis EXISTS plus LRANGE on snippets:<lang>:featured — and then Trinket.findByIds against MongoDB; lib/controllers/trinket.js:L53-L55 assigns the result to data.trinkets. python is the only enabled trinket type, so GET /python performs that read and returns 200 while the other ten landings 404 at trinketTypeEnabled first. The authenticated supplement reads state as well, through pages.home -> Trinket.findRecentByOwner. Two controls were then measured. Seeding snippets:python:featured with one real Trinket — verified to resolve, byCategory returning the id and findByIds returning the document — produced ZERO differences across all 65 entries, left the normalized GET /python body byte-identical at 13926 bytes and digest e6afbb9b6444a8ea19c1148d9478fe5c32a067f10e1f7d0d06ce0dad4ca317ba, and the seeded document's id, name and slug appeared in NONE of the 63 raw bodies, because no template in trinket/python/python.html -> trinket/python/base.html -> base.html reads the `trinkets` context variable. Giving the throwaway identity one owned Trinket, by contrast, changed exactly two fields on exactly one entry: authenticated GET /home content-length 18126 -> 18448 and its bodyShape digest.
adjudications.resolution: Both halves of the fix are applied, and neither is a normalization. (1) selectionRule.rationale no longer claims datastore independence and now says precisely what the filter does guarantee — fixture independence. (2) The capture is performed against dedicated ephemeral MongoDB and Redis instances on non-colliding ports, explicitly initialized out of band before boot and fingerprinted before and after, all recorded in metadata.datastoreState together with the featured-region determinism rule a replay must honour. No structural normalization of the featured region is introduced, because measurement shows none is required: the region is inert in every recorded field. The one genuinely state-sensitive entry is named in metadata.datastoreState.stateSensitiveEntries and its inputs are pinned in metadata.throwawayUser.
